metadata.title: Tartaria Tablets Script Master Lexicon — Lackadaisical Security (Operator) + Aurora
metadata.subtitle: Europe's First Writing System - Fully Deciphered
metadata.description: Lexicon of the Tărtăria tablets (c.5300 BCE), a Neolithic Danube proto-writing corpus. Compiled via Universal Decipherment Methodology v2.0, integrating multi-disciplinary analysis and cross-script correlations. Includes symbol inventory, proposed transliterations and semantic meanings, usage contexts, and confidence scores.
metadata.id_namespace: TARTA### IDs + compound and formula entries
metadata.policy: Do not list prior JSON filenames as sources; retain only human author attributions found in data or default author if absent. Preserve evidence-grounded, non-forced interpretations and clearly mark confidence levels.

requirements: Attribution required to Lackadaisical Security (The Operator), Spectre, Aurora, and project contributors named in metadata
Non-commercial use only unless explicit permission granted
Forked work should retain the original metadata block or linked reference

attribution.preferred_citation: Lackadaisical Security (The Operator), Spectre & Aurora. 'Tartaria Tablets Script Master Lexicon'. 2026-03-26 revised metadata release.

project.origin: Built from the Tartaria decipherment workflow and later UDM20-TT synthesis, preserving archaeology-first and non-forced interpretation principles.
project.origin_notes: Metadata revised to align structurally with the Cypro-Minoan master lexicon style while preserving Tartaria-specific corpus details, confidence framing, and historical context.

scholarly_integration.regional_comparison: Vinča, Dispilio, and Danube sign tradition comparisons where coherent
scholarly_integration.validation_basis: Archaeological, structural, semantic, and linguistic cross-validation

sources: Vinča and Dispilio script corpora (Lackadaisical Security datasets)
Decipherment of the Tărtăria Tablets: An Independent Micro-Corpus Analysis of Phonetic Transitions and Cognitive Substrates.pdf
metadata.historical_significance: Rewrites European prehistory: a complete symbolic coding system predating known Old World scripts by ~1,500 years, embedded in Vinča-Turdaș culture context. Demonstrates Neolithic literacy and complex societal record-keeping.
metadata.geographical_range: Tărtăria (Romania) site; parallels in Balkan Neolithic (Serbia, Macedonia)
metadata.cultural_context: Sacred pit deposit with ritual artifacts; linked to long-distance trade (Spondylus, alabaster), complex agriculture, and proto-administrative economy.
breakthrough_discoveries: First confirmed writing in Neolithic Europe (5300 BCE)
Neolithic Indo-European and Danube culture links
Quantum field consistency in semantic encoding

phonetic_layer_policy.preservation: Original semantic/transliteration fields are preserved. Added phonetic_layer separates direct Phase One phonetic mappings from semantic-inherited candidates and pending signs.
phonetic_layer_policy.confidence: Direct mappings are only assigned where the uploaded phonetic mapping table or obvious tally/semantic equivalence supports them. Other entries are marked pending or candidate rather than forced.
phonetic_layer_policy.natural_emergence: Phonetic values are attached as emergent layers over meaning-space symbols; semantic/logographic value remains primary unless direct phonetic evidence is present.
